item.title: What exactly is "birth tourism?"
item.description: President Trump signed two executive orders targeting birthright citizenship and "birth tourism." The latter is an issue that Trump has raised for years.

item.title: The U.S. unexpectedly lost jobs in July
item.description: The U.S. labor market went into reverse last month, as employers cut 23,000 jobs. Job gains for May and June were also revised downward.
item.content:encoded: The U.S. labor market went into reverse last month, as employers cut 23,000 jobs. Job gains for May and June were also revised downward.

item.title: Redistricting played a part in Tennessee's primary election results
item.description: Tennessee's primary election put its redistricting from earlier this year on display at the ballot box as results questioned President Trump's endorsement.

item.title: Staff at the CDC in Atlanta remember victim of shooting a year ago as RFK jr. attends
item.description: It's been a year since a gunman opened fire on the CDC and killed a security guard. RFK Jr. visited the CDC today to remember the victim.

item.title: A new investigative podcast uncovers new evidence in death of young BLM protester
item.description: "We Keep Us Safe," a new investigative podcast series from Embedded, uncovered new evidence in the 2020 shooting death of 16-year-old Antonio Mays Jr. -- a killing that remains unsolved.

item.title: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is outpacing responders
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is now the second largest ever, and shows no sign of slowing down. To help, researchers are trying to expand experimental vaccines and treatments

item.title: Deadheads forever: The long legacy of the Grateful Dead's fan community
item.description: As part of NPR Music's series The Ripple Effect, Isabella Gomez Sarmiento speaks with Deadheads young and old, including famous followers like reality TV host Andy Cohen, who saw his first Grateful Dead show as a teenager in 1986, and young fans just discovering the band -- and passing on their appreciation to others.

item.title: What the dwindling U.S. missile stock means for the future
item.description: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with Phillips Payson O'Brien from the University of St. Andrews about the implications of reports that the U.S. is running low on weapons.
